stemMarkdown: Two runners start together from the same point on a circular track 1000 m long and run in the same direction at 12 km/h and 5 km/h. After how many seconds does the faster runner first lap the slower one? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: In the same direction the speeds subtract: $1.9444$ m/s. To meet again the faster runner must gain a full lap of 1000 m, which takes $\dfrac{1000}{1.9444} = 514.2857$ seconds.
altSolutionMarkdown: Meeting on a circle means the gap between them has grown to exactly one whole lap.
